text:
Sasha: Morning — cron `nightly-eval-smoke` failed on the eval runner, timed out on the alloc-benchmark step. CI: https://ci.redwood/invoke/12345

ci-bot: Build 12345 — step eval-smoke failed (exit code 124). Logs: /artifacts/12345/logs

Sasha: snippet from logs:
```
2026-03-16T05:12:40Z ERROR RunTimeoutError: benchmark step exceeded 1800s
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/eval/runner.py", line 210, in run_bench
    result = worker.execute()
  File "/app/eval/worker.py", line 78, in execute
    raise RunTimeoutError()
RunTimeoutError
```

Matt: is this the same flake we saw last week?

Jen: maybe — last time s3 list throttling caused a hang in the bootstrap. @Liam any idea?

Liam: looking. I see a spike in 03:00 S3 503s around the same time. I'll bump the client's backoff and restart the cron.

Sasha: can someone trigger a rerun after restart? I'll queue it if needed.

Matt: if it's S3 we should also add a short retry wrapper in the eval harness. Filing a quick PR after this: https://github.com/redwood/eval/pull/789

Liam: restarted the cron runner and increased retries. Kicking rerun: https://ci.redwood/invoke/12346

ci-bot: Rerun 12346 started.

ci-bot: Rerun 12346 SUCCESS — eval-smoke passed.

Sasha: great — closing the incident. Jen/Matt please keep PR in review; I'll add the incident notes to the oncall doc.

Jen: ack :thumbsup:

Matt: thanks all.
